clue.text: Approach made by firm to this writer

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, a business firm
the setter speaking of themself in the first person gives me

explanation.surface: A business firm sends an offer to the person writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to draw near, which is what coming does.

clue.text: Bird's convenience food that may pose a nasty problem

definitions.meaning: a tinned meal ready to hand for a bird that eats grubs
an idiom for a messy situation that, once opened up, brings a host of complications

explanation.surface: A packaged meal for a bird turns out to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird's is also a British brand of custard powder, a convenience food, which pulls the solver the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a tin full of wriggling grubs is the image behind the idiom for an awkward, complicated predicament.

clue.text: Minds used to be sparking now there's confusion

indicators.note: minds that are sparking fire off in all directions, so these letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Once-brilliant minds have now lost their focus.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddiness of thought is murkiness, a lack of clarity, a muddle.

clue.text: Face one's sin with difficulty, avoiding a revelation?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Face one's sin with difficulty, avoiding a revelation? (10)': the evident parse (anagram of FACE ONE'S SIN less A) gives two Es and one O where CONFESSION needs one E and two Os; no scan, and a search found no other text or parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Face one's sin with difficulty, avoiding a revelation?

clue.text: Crime of thief's accomplice

parts.note: a fence is a receiver who buys stolen goods from a thief and sells them on

explanation.surface: Helping a burglar is itself a criminal act.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as held reads 'chief's', a one-letter misreading of 'thief's': a fence is a thief's partner, not a chief's.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, a criminal act.

clue.text: Agents brought in convenient invention

indicators.note: brought in means the agents' word is placed inside the word for convenient

parts.note: fit, as in a fit time, means suitable or convenient
G-men are FBI agents in American slang, short for government men

explanation.surface: FBI agents are drafted into a handy fabrication.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something made up or imagined, a fiction of the mind.

clue.text: Band music that could celebrate a thirtieth anniversary?

definitions.text: Band music that could celebrate a thirtieth anniversary?

parts.words: Band music that could celebrate a thirtieth anniversary?
parts.note: Glenn Miller's big band had a 1941 hit of this name, and pearl is the traditional gift for thirty years of marriage, so a necklace would mark the occasion

explanation.surface: A dance band plays a tune at a couple's thirtieth wedding party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' first suggests a group of musicians, but a necklace is also a band of beads.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glenn Miller swing classic shares its name with a necklace, and pearl is the gift for a thirtieth wedding anniversary.

clue.text: Remarkably solid objects such as the Golden Calf

definitions.text: objects such as the Golden Calf

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of solid are turned out in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Statues of gold like the biblical calf are strikingly sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Calf was a false god the Israelites worshipped, an image venerated in place of the deity.

clue.text: Teaching union's crackers

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
the possessive ending supplies its letter S

explanation.surface: The teachers' union has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers and nuts are both British slang for crazy.

clue.text: A maxim that isn't true for the successful writer of detective stories?

definitions.text: A maxim that isn't true for the successful writer of detective stories?

parts.words: A maxim that isn't true for the successful writer of detective stories?
parts.note: a best-selling author of whodunits profits from wrongdoing on the page, so a familiar proverb about lawbreaking fails for them

explanation.surface: A successful mystery author disproves a well-known saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says lawbreaking never brings reward, yet a best-selling author of detective fiction earns a living from it.

clue.text: One man suffering setback — little right — lowest point

indicators.note: one man suffering a setback is sent backwards, so the pair of words reads in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Dan is a man's name
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: A man has a bad turn of fortune and hits rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'little right' look like an aside, but it is just a final letter added to the turned-round man.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom-most point, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Bodily shape's deficient, understand?

parts.note: a figure is the shape of a person's body; the 's is a link standing for 'is'
out can mean lacking or short, as in 'we're out of milk'

explanation.surface: Someone frets that their physique is lacking, and asks if others get it.
explanation.definitionFit: To work a thing out is to grasp it, so understanding and puzzling through mean the same.

clue.text: Gentlemen preferring blondes? Not an example of this, say brunettes!

definitions.text: Gentlemen preferring blondes? Not an example of this, say brunettes!

parts.words: Gentlemen preferring blondes? Not an example of this, say brunettes!
parts.note: fair means both blonde and just, so men who favour blonde hair show bias, and dark-haired women would call them anything but impartial

explanation.surface: Dark-haired women accuse men who favour blondes of bias.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the film title Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being even-handed means judging without bias, and a preference for one hair colour is a bias.

clue.text: Aloofness of some engaged in military action?

definitions.meaning: a cool, distant manner, standing apart from others
a small body of troops split off from the main force for a particular operation

explanation.surface: Is aloofness typical of soldiers engaged in battle?
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional distance is aloofness, and a squad of soldiers sent off on a mission bears the same name.

clue.text: Finished fight, ending prematurely or late?

parts.note: over means finished, as in 'the game is over'

indicators.note: ending prematurely means the word for fight stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a duel is a formal fight between two people

explanation.surface: A bout that was stopped early: was it finished on time or late?
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has passed the time it was expected, so it is behind schedule.

clue.text: The foreign currency he spent brings inconvenience

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so he is removed from the word before it

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Spending the foreign money he had brought causes him bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he spent' takes HE out of THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble and inconvenience both mean bother or difficulty caused to someone.

clue.text: Combative celeb is left floundering with nothing gained

indicators.note: gained means taken on board, so the letter for nothing is put inside the jumbled letters
floundering means struggling clumsily, so these letters thrash about into a new order

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A celebrity, flailing and abandoned, turns aggressive with nothing to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floundering' gives BELLICSE; 'gained' sets O in the gap after BELLIC. 'nothing gained' reads like a complaint about wasted effort, but it is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose describes someone eager to fight, warlike in temper.

clue.text: Boys stare naughtily when Ms comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the letters of Ms surround the jumbled ones
naughtily suggests misbehaving letters that will not stay in order

explanation.surface: Schoolboys gawp mischievously when a female teacher walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' gives ASTER, which 'comes round' sets between M and S. Master is an old-fashioned formal title for a boy, as on an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Master is the polite title for a young lad, as on an envelope, so lads can be called this.

clue.text: A bit of a fruitcake, this mistress?

definitions.meaning: a seedless dried grape, one of the pieces of fruit in a fruitcake
a wife or concubine of a Muslim ruler; the question mark admits the stretch

explanation.surface: Is this mistress a little bit crazy?
explanation.definitionFit: A dried white grape baked into fruitcakes shares its name with a sultan's wife or consort.

clue.text: A mother getting Rick to imbibe from old flask

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the mother's word takes the other inside it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to rick is to wrench or strain a muscle, the same as to pull one

explanation.surface: A mother persuades someone called Rick to drink from an antique bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to strain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampulla was a small two-handled vessel used in ancient Rome for oils or wine.

clue.text: Invite a nice one put

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Invite a nice one put (7)': ASK (invite) + A NICE less I (one) gives the letters, but there is no definition and the clue ends mid-phrase (probably 'put out' plus a word like 'sideways'); no scan, and a search found no fuller text.

clue.text: Be as one that has gills — and gills!

definitions.text: Be as one that has gills — and gills!

parts.words: Be as one that has gills — and gills!
parts.note: gills are a fish's breathing organs, and a gill is also a quarter-pint measure of drink, so a heavy drinker downs gills

explanation.surface: Breathe like a sea creature, and down plenty of small measures too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes drinking alcohol to excess, as a fish seems to swallow water constantly.

clue.text: Study English novelist

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: Research an author from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian writer of fiction, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.

clue.text: One may catch new sort of disease

indicators.note: catch means hold inside, so the word for one encloses the letter for new

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Someone might contract a novel kind of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin complaint of inflamed spots and pimples.

clue.text: Member of the clergy holding Mass for French explorer

indicators.note: holding means the clergyman's word wraps around the letter for Mass

parts.note: a chaplain is a priest attached to a chapel, regiment or institution
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A priest celebrates Mass on behalf of a French adventurer.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec and charted much of New France in the early 1600s.

clue.text: Free toilets at end of lane

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: at end of picks out the final letter of lane

explanation.surface: Public toilets at the end of the street cost nothing to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unconfined or at liberty, as an animal running loose.

clue.text: Mere yapper must change to become smoother

indicators.note: must change says the letters of mere yapper are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog that does nothing but bark needs to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoother' looks like an adjective about calmer behaviour but is a noun: something that smooths.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery paper is an abrasive sheet used to sand surfaces, so it is a tool for smoothing.

clue.text: The Yorkshire hospital department's temporary accommodation

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is clipped to t', as in 'on t' moor'
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire hospital ward makes do with makeshift lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent is a canvas shelter put up for a short stay, such as camping.
